item.title: Systolic Geometry and Combinatorics of Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.40750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This thesis investigates two themes. The first studies systolic embeddings of graph on translation surfaces, proving existence results for essential and cellular systolic embeddings and determining extremal genera for certain graph families. The second examines hyperbolic surfaces in the Thurston set, constructing a one-parameter deformation that increases the sys- tole length and produces Bolza-like surfaces, i.e., surfaces whose systolic geodesics decompose the surfaces into triangles, for infinitely many genera. A symmetry property of geodesic inter- sections on these surfaces is also established, together with an application of these Bolza-like surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Achintya Dey

item.title: Exotic involutions on irreducible 4-manifolds from Real Seiberg--Witten theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.40802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using Real Seiberg--Witten theory, Miyazawa constructed infinitely many exotic involutions on ${\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$, and Baraglia extended this construction to $X\#{\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$ for a broad class of $4$-manifolds $X$ equipped with an involution $c$. We show that, under suitable Real Seiberg--Witten hypotheses, the ${\overline{\mathbb{CP}}{}^2}$ summand can be omitted when $X$ is non-spin and the complement of the fixed locus is simply-connected. Our construction also yields infinite families of topologically isotopic but smoothly non-isotopic embeddings of the branch surface in the quotient $X/\langle c\rangle$. As applications, we construct anti-holomorphic involutions on irreducible, simply-connected projective surfaces of general type with infinitely many exotic copies, none of which is anti-symplectic with respect to any orientation-compatible symplectic form. These surfaces include cyclic branched covers of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and complete intersections of multidegree $(2,4k)$ in $\mathbb{CP}^4$.
item.dc:creator: Woohyeok Jo, Simone Tagliente

item.title: On lens spaces which may embed in the complex projective plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.40957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using an obstruction derived by Owens and relying on Donaldson's Diagonalisation Theorem, we obtain a complete classification of lens spaces of Lisca type $(2)$ or $(3)$ that are unobstructed from embedding in a homology complex projective plane. This classification is further refined for lens spaces $L(p,q)$ with $p$ even, using an obstruction due to Lidman--Moore--Vazquez based on work of Lin. This article is extracted from the author's PhD thesis.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Carfora

item.title: Handlebodies separate elements of surface groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note I prove that every non-trivial element of the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface X is non-trivial in the fundamental group of some handlebody with boundary X. This result appears to be folklore. I have uploaded a proof as the result is needed in a joint project with Clement Dupont on mapping class group actions on configuration spaces.
item.dc:creator: Richard Hain

item.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.41002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Malo Gatignol, Joe Thomas

item.title: The Table Problem for Convex Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.41010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a generalized Table Theorem for bounded convex domains in the plane. Then we prove a variation of the Table Problem for compactly supported functions on the plane. Our method is based on relating the table problem on a surface to the square peg problem for a configuration of star-shaped curves in the tangent bundle of the surface.
item.dc:creator: Ali Naseri Sadr

item.title: Rationally slice knots that are not biprojectively H-slice
item.description: arXiv:2610.41996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that rationally slice knots need not be biprojectively H-slice (BPH-slice), answering a question in the study of the rational knot concordance group. Our main tool is a lattice embedding obstruction to H-sliceness in $\#^n\mathbb{CP}^2$ for knots with vanishing signature, extending work of Kjuchukova--Miller--Ray--Sakall{\i}. We apply the obstruction to an infinite family of rationally slice knots, beginning with $8_{18}$. As additional applications, we obstruct the BPH-sliceness of a family of 2-bridge knots which is not obstructed by the instanton knot concordance invariant $r_0$, we obstruct a non-alternating family of Montesinos knots, and we give prime alternating knots that are topologically but not smoothly biprojectively H-slice. We discuss why these knots remain plausible candidates for detecting exotic smooth structures on $\#^n\mathbb{CP}^2$ and suggest natural sources of further candidates.
item.dc:creator: Elise Brod

item.title: Constructing Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from multi-grid diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2610.42076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a new diagrammatic construction of Lagrangian surfaces in all symplectic toric $4$-manifolds from objects called multi-grid diagrams. These are a generalisation of triple grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ wherein the underlying trisection is replaced by the more general notion of a toric decomposition. We give examples of multi-grid diagrams for Lagrangian surfaces in a range of symplectic toric $4$-manifolds, including Evans' recent non-squeezable Klein bottle in $S^2 \times S^2$.
item.dc:creator: Shintaro Fushida-Hardy, Laura Wakelin

item.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Links
item.description: arXiv:2610.42077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every link in the \(3\)-sphere admits a generalised \(T\)-link presentation. In this paper, we give an explicit polynomial-time algorithm which, given a signed Artin braid word and the number of strands, computes such a presentation. Combining this construction with Yamada--Vogel braiding gives a polynomial-time conversion from arbitrary oriented combinatorial link diagrams to generalised \(T\)-link parameters. We prove polynomial bounds on the number of strands and crossings in the resulting braid. As an application, we prove that a link property or a link invariant is computable in polynomial time from diagrams if and only if the corresponding problem is solvable in polynomial time from generalised \(T\)-link parameters, with parameter input measured by the total number of strands and crossings in the corresponding braid diagram. Whenever a classification criterion or an explicit invariant formula is available in these parameters, it can be applied to the original link by substituting the parameters obtained from the diagram. A polynomial-time test or evaluation then gives a polynomial-time procedure on diagrams. We also establish the corresponding transfer for approximating real-valued invariants to prescribed accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Thiago de Paiva, Yi Liu

item.title: Holonomies of hyperbolic surfaces with one branch point
item.description: arXiv:2610.42079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. We prove that any representation of $\pi_1(S)$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ with Euler class $3-2g$ is the holonomy of a hyperbolic metric on $S$ with one simple branch point.
item.dc:creator: Bertrand Deroin, Nicolas Tholozan

item.title: Orientations for skein-valued curve counting
item.description: arXiv:2610.41233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention. We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.
item.dc:creator: Brett Parker

item.title: A local-to-global fixed point theorem for $\CAT(0)$ spaces with a uniform elliptic gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.41468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A finitely generated group acting locally elliptically on a complete \CAT(0) space of finite geometric dimension fixes a point if distances to elliptic fixed sets are uniformly controlled by displacements. For arbitrary groups, the same hypothesis gives a fixed point in the space or its visual boundary. The proof combines a first-moment random-walk displacement estimate with Izeki's zero-drift theorem. For finite-rank $\R$-buildings whose Euclidean metric factor has finite linear image, we obtain an all-type local-to-global theorem, including the nondiscrete $\widetilde G_2$ case, with an explicit gap and without metric completeness; the linear-image restriction can be removed from the fixed-point conclusion when the Euclidean factor has dimension at most three. A tangent-cone criterion characterizes the gap and yields a cubical bound with optimal asymptotic growth $d/\pi$ in dimension $d$. For Hadamard manifolds, the gap is equivalent to uniformly bounded finite stabilizers in the isometry image, with stabilizer bounds of optimal polynomial growth in the gap constant.
item.dc:creator: Jeroen Schillewaert

item.title: Geometrization of almost extremal representations in $\text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$
item.description: arXiv:1802.00755v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S$ be a closed surface of genus $g$. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between hyperbolic cone-structure on $S$ and representations of the fundamental group into $\text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$. We consider surfaces of genus greater than $g$ and we show that, under suitable conditions, every representation $\rho:\pi_1 S\longrightarrow \text{PSL}_2\Bbb R$ with Euler number $\mathcal{E}(\rho)=\pm\big(\chi(S)+1\big)$ arises as holonomy of a hyperbolic cone-structure $\sigma$ on $S$ with a single cone point of angle $4\pi$. From this result, we derive that for surfaces of genus $2$ every representation with $\mathcal{E}(\rho)=\pm1$ arises as the holonomy of some hyperbolic cone-structure.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Faraco

item.title: Exotic $\mathbb{R}^4$'s with Compactly Supported Diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2508.02017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that for diffeomorphisms of closed simply-connected $4$-manifolds dissolving under a single stabilization, there is a natural induced diffeomorphism on an exotic copy of $\RR^4$. We thereby construct uncountably many exotic copies of $\RR^4$ with nontrivial compactly supported mapping class groups of arbitrarily large rank. This follows from a modification of the construction of the diffeomorphism corks of arXiv:2407.04696 that makes their exteriors simply-connected.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Shivkumar

item.title: Achiral Lefschetz fibrations and the moduli space of curves
item.description: arXiv:2510.18593v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Symplectic Lefschetz fibrations can be described via classifying maps with values in the Deligne-Mumford compactification of the moduli space of curves, by means of constructions relying on symplectic geometry. In this note we prove the existence of classifying maps for achiral Lefschetz fibrations using Riemannian geometry. We further extend Smith's signature formula to the achiral case, providing a more elementary proof of this statement.
item.dc:creator: Sardor Yakupov

item.title: Integrals of general geometric random variables on the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.23626v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article we provide an integration formula enabling us to integrate random variables defined on the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces which involve the lengths of closed geodesics of any prescribed topological type, at fixed genus and number of boundaries. We then compute the general form of length functions of closed loops in Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates. Using this expression together with our integration formula, we express the expectations of geometric random variables as integrals over R with almost polynomial density. As a consequence, given an arbitrary closed loop $\gamma$, we obtain an improvement of Mirzakhani's asymptotic equivalent of the Weil-Petersson expectation E[N$\gamma$(a)], when a $\rightarrow$ $\infty$, of the number of geodesics with same topological type as $\gamma$ of length at most a. We finally provide, for a loop $\gamma$ filling a one-holed torus or a four-holed sphere, an interpretation of the density function associated with $\gamma$ as the period of the Hamiltonian flow of the length function of $\gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Victor Le Guilloux (IMJ-PRG)

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28986v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay
